analyst.summary: PNB Housing Finance has turned around its asset quality (GNPA down to sub-1% from over 8% four years ago) and is growing its retail book at a healthy mid-teens pace, funded comfortably by a strong capital base and a fresh AAA credit-rating upgrade. FY26 profit growth was flattered by one-off loan recoveries that will not repeat, so we would expect FY27 profit growth to run a bit below the 18-20% loan-book growth management is guiding to. At about 12-13x earnings and 1.5x book for a ~13% ROE lender, the stock looks fairly priced for what it is - a well-capitalized, much-improved but not exceptional-return housing financier - so we recommend holding rather than adding or exiting on fundamentals alone.
